summary: Across all 315 past IPOs, 71% closed their first day up (median +12%). That's the coin-flip to beat: a score is only useful if its groups do better or worse than this.
Listing-day scores of 70 and up: 85% closed up (median +28%), against 50% for Under 40 (median -1%).
The check that best told apart IPOs that closed their first day up: “Are big investors keen?” (43 points between Good and Warning).
The check that best told apart IPOs that beat the Nifty 50 over a year: “Are big investors keen?” (34 points between Good and Warning).
caveats: Each score uses only what was known on the IPO's closing day: its offer document, the final bids, the market that day and IPOs that had already listed. Nothing from after, so the test is fair.

IPOs without their RHP added are scored on demand and market mood alone: the engine still works out a score, but calls it too little data for a verdict. Each group says how many had enough; add RHPs to fill the rest in.
Past results don't promise future ones: markets change, and a few IPOs per group is a small sample.
Returns are price only, from the issue price, with splits and bonus shares counted; dividends are left out for the IPO and the Nifty alike.
